source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Aurora is Illinois' largest disclosed IT capacity at 114 megawatts, representing 48 percent of the state's published data center power.

The campus spans three buildings and 450,000 square feet, yielding about 6.3 megawatts per 10,000 square feet, a density typical of hyperscale colocation built in the last decade. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 114 megawatts translates to roughly 2,850 racks. That is a substantial power budget for compute, but it is a capacity figure, not evidence that the site can run modern accelerator clusters.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, yet only six disclose power figures, and this campus accounts for nearly half of all disclosed capacity. The concentration means public understanding of the state's data center power is dominated by one operator. The published specifications omit total campus power draw, PUE, renewable sourcing, grid connection characteristics, cooling technology, and interconnect uplinks. Without those facts, the campus's role in AI scaling cannot be assessed: its power budget may be grid-constrained, its cooling may not sustain accelerator thermal density, and its connectivity may not absorb training workloads.
